## Complete case analysis {.smaller}

How many countries do we have in the data?
```{r}
length(unique(finaldata$iso))
```
How many countries do we have if we perform complete case analysis on the outcome maternal mortality?
```{r}
matmordata <- finaldata |> dplyr::select(-infant_mortality, -under5_mortality, -neonatal_mortality)
completedata <- matmordata[complete.cases(matmordata),]
length(unique(completedata$iso))
```
How many countries do we have if we perform complete case analysis on the outcome child mortality?
```{r}
childmordata <- finaldata |> dplyr::select(-maternal_mortality)
completedata <- childmordata[complete.cases(childmordata),]
length(unique(completedata$iso))
```
How many countries are listed in the original armed conflict paper?


## Regression models of interest

We fit the following four models last week
```{r}
preds <- as.formula(" ~ armed_conflict + loggdp + oecd + pop_dens + urban +
              age_dep + male_edu + temp + rainfall_1000 + earthquake + drought")

matmormod <- plm(update.formula(preds, maternal_mortality ~ .), index = c("iso", "year"), effect = "twoways",
                 model = "within", data = finaldata)
un5mormod <- plm(update.formula(preds, under5_mortality ~ .), index = c("iso", "year"), effect = "twoways",
                 model = "within", data = finaldata)
infmormod <- plm(update.formula(preds, infant_mortality ~ .), index = c("iso", "year"), effect = "twoways",
                 model = "within", data = finaldata)
neomormod <- plm(update.formula(preds, neonatal_mortality ~ .), index = c("iso", "year"), effect = "twoways",
                 model = "within", data = finaldata)
```

## Considerations before running MI {.smaller}

- Are any variables MNAR? 
- If all variables are MCAR, do we need to perform MI?
- Variables are repeatedly measured over time. Which variables are level 1? Level 2?
- GDP was log transformed. Do we use GDP in the imputation model then transform or use log(GDP) in the imputation model?
- Can we impute the outcome variables?
  + MI doesn't know which variables are outcomes or predictors
  + There is an ongoing debate in the literature about whether to use imputed outcome variable in the analysis
  + One approach is "multiple imputation then deletion" (MID) where the outcome variable is included in the imputation model but outcome values that were initially missing are omitted in the analysis
  + MID requires additional coding... could use an R package **(\*\*Hint Hint\*\*)**
  + Additional readings: [Paper 1](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00223891.2018.1530680), [Paper 2](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cjca.2020.11.010)



## Apply MI 

- Need to convert `iso` to numeric
```{r}
midata <- finaldata |>
  mutate(iso_num = as.numeric(as.factor(finaldata$iso))) |>
  select(-iso)
```

- Dry run to get `meth` and `pred`
```{r}
mice0  <- mice(midata, seed = 100, m = 5, maxit = 0, print = F)
```
- Edit `meth` and `pred`
```{r}
meth <- mice0$method
meth[c("urban", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000", "loggdp", "pop_dens",
       "maternal_mortality", "infant_mortality", "neonatal_mortality", "under5_mortality")] <- "2l.lmer"

pred <- mice0$predictorMatrix
pred[c("urban", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000", "loggdp", "pop_dens",
       "maternal_mortality", "infant_mortality", "neonatal_mortality", "under5_mortality"), "iso_num"] <- -2
```


## Perform MI with `mice` package

- First, let's quickly perform MI with `m=2` imputations
```{r}
mice.multi.out  <- mice(midata, seed = 100, m = 10, maxit = 20,
                        method = meth,
                        predictorMatrix = pred)

```
## Perform MI with `mice` package

- Check for convergence
```{r}
plot(mice.multi.out)
```

## Saving MI output

- It's a good idea to save the MI output as an R object

```{r}
#| eval: false

save(mice.multi.out, file = "output//mice_out.RData")
```



## Fit model 

- Fit the four regression models on the 2 imputed data sets using the `with()` function
  + Unfortunately `plm()` cannot be used within `with()` so need to use `lm()`
  + But, can we use `plm()` on multiply imputed data? It would be nice to have a package that does this... **(\*\*Hint Hint\*\*)**
  
```{r}
# Maternal mortality
fit.mi.matmor <- with(mice.multi.out, 
  lm(maternal_mortality ~ -1 + armed_conflict_lagged + loggdp + oecd + pop_dens + urban + 
       age_dep + male_edu + temp + rainfall_1000 + earthquake + drought + 
       as.factor(iso_num) + as.factor(year)))

# Under-5 mortality
fit.mi.un5 <- with(mice.multi.out, 
  lm(under5_mortality ~ -1 + armed_conflict_lagged + loggdp + oecd + pop_dens + urban + 
       age_dep + male_edu + temp + rainfall_1000 + earthquake + drought + 
       as.factor(iso_num) + as.factor(year)))

# Infant mortality
fit.mi.inf <- with(mice.multi.out, 
  lm(infant_mortality ~ -1 + armed_conflict_lagged + loggdp + oecd + pop_dens + urban + 
       age_dep + male_edu + temp + rainfall_1000 + earthquake + drought + 
       as.factor(iso_num) + as.factor(year)))

# Neonatal mortality
fit.mi.neo <- with(mice.multi.out, 
  lm(neonatal_mortality ~ -1 + armed_conflict_lagged + loggdp + oecd + pop_dens + urban + 
       age_dep + male_edu + temp + rainfall_1000 + earthquake + drought + 
       as.factor(iso_num) + as.factor(year)))
```

## Summarize results 

- Use the `pool()` function to apply Rubin's rules to summarize the regression estimates and standard errors
```{r}
out.mi.matmor <- pool(fit.mi.matmor)
out.mi.un5 <- pool(fit.mi.un5)
out.mi.inf <- pool(fit.mi.inf)
out.mi.neo <- pool(fit.mi.neo)
```

- `summary()` function will produce a table with estimates, standard errors, etc. 

```{r}
summary(out.mi.matmor)
summary(out.mi.un5)
summary(out.mi.inf)
summary(out.mi.neo)
```

```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------
# Question 3: Compare complete-case and MI results
# --------------------------------------------------

# 1. Define the predictors to include (exclude fixed effects)
predictors <- c(
  "armed_conflict_lagged", "loggdp", "oecd", "pop_dens",
  "urban", "age_dep", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000",
  "earthquake", "drought"
)

# 2. Extract complete-case regression results
extract_cc <- function(model, outcome) {

  estimates <- coef(model)
  intervals <- confint(model)

  tibble(
    outcome = outcome,
    term = names(estimates),
    estimate = as.numeric(estimates),
    lower = intervals[names(estimates), 1],
    upper = intervals[names(estimates), 2]
  )
}

cc_results <- bind_rows(
  extract_cc(matmormod, "Maternal mortality"),
  extract_cc(un5mormod, "Under-5 mortality"),
  extract_cc(infmormod, "Infant mortality"),
  extract_cc(neomormod, "Neonatal mortality")
) |>
  filter(term %in% predictors)

# 3. Extract pooled multiple-imputation results
extract_mi <- function(model, outcome) {

  results <- summary(model, conf.int = TRUE)

  tibble(
    outcome = outcome,
    term = results$term,
    estimate = results$estimate,
    lower = results$`2.5 %`,
    upper = results$`97.5 %`
  )
}

mi_results <- bind_rows(
  extract_mi(out.mi.matmor, "Maternal mortality"),
  extract_mi(out.mi.un5, "Under-5 mortality"),
  extract_mi(out.mi.inf, "Infant mortality"),
  extract_mi(out.mi.neo, "Neonatal mortality")
) |>
  filter(term %in% predictors)

# 4. Format complete-case results
cc_table <- cc_results |>
  mutate(
    CC = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", estimate, lower, upper)
  ) |>
  select(outcome, term, CC)

# 5. Format multiple-imputation results
mi_table <- mi_results |>
  mutate(
    MI = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", estimate, lower, upper)
  ) |>
  select(outcome, term, MI)

# 6. Combine both sets of results
comparison_table <- full_join(
  cc_table,
  mi_table,
  by = c("outcome", "term")
)

# 7. Display the final table
comparison_table

# 8. Save the table as a CSV file
write.csv(
  comparison_table,
  "output/CC_vs_MI_comparison.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
